regenerationJustification.cite: tdd SS3.4 (turn/interrupt: the user's stop gesture on the priority lane; it stops the ACTIVE turn and does not consume a pre-queued successor, the #16579 owner ruling), SS3.5 (on either stop lane, work queued behind the turn may still start at its terminal), SS3.2 (turn/start with ifBusy queue: the ack pre-mints the turn, disposition queued), SS3.1.1 and SS4.13 (queue movement: a client holding an acked-queued entry re-verifies it by replaying its commandId, answered with the original ack; the entry materializes at its own turn/started); the host's session-boundary pin interrupt_spares_queued_launch (spec 207 TEST-017); the recipe charter is #22934 (cancellation: interactive interruption with a queued successor); #104154 (the burst order committed so CI guards the wire-order check of #104021)
regenerationJustification.rationale: The turn-interrupt-queued-successor exchange, frame for frame, with one difference: the queued turn's turn/started is written right after the stopped turn's cancelled terminal, before the client's SS4.13 queue-movement replay and its original-ack answer. That is the burst a live host may produce, because it launches the queued turn when the stopped turn reaches its terminal without waiting for the replay (SS3.5), and the sibling's manifest already names this interleaving as legal; serve-fixture then writes the terminal and the launch in one burst where the sibling's request/reply handshake forces a chunk boundary between them. The cookbook cancel recipe's interrupt arm runs on both files, so a check that reads the handle after an await instead of the order of the frames on the wire (#104021) fails here while it passes on the sibling (#104154). Every frame, identifier, cursor and timestamp is the sibling's; only the position of the replay exchange against the launch differs.
